datasets.name: Destinations
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Built by authors from University of Notre Dame network traffic (summer 2004), aggregated per destination host; hosts receiving SNORT-flagged packets labeled compromised; SNORT attack types collapsed into a 2-class problem (intrusive vs not) (p.2)

datasets.name: Packets
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Built by authors from University of Notre Dame network packets (summer 2004) with SNORT labels; attack types collapsed into a 2-class problem (intrusive vs not) (p.2)

chosen.metric: ROC curve (%TP vs %FP); no G-mean/AUC/F1/accuracy values printed
chosen.condition: Packets dataset, 75/25 train/test split, majority undersampled to sweep ROC; Cluster-SMOTE with 3 and 5 k-means clusters vs 500 SMOTE

win_claim.quote: we establish that our clustering based approach is more suitable for the detecting intrusions and is able to provide additional improvement over just synthetic generation of instances.

uncertain: how_obtained set to 'modified' because authors constructed the datasets and collapsed SNORT alert types into 2 classes; could alternatively be considered 'original' (p.2)
Cluster-SMOTE was compared to SMOTE only on Packets (Fig. 4, p.5); on Destinations clustering yielded a single cluster so no Cluster-SMOTE comparison exists (p.6)

No numeric per-dataset results; comparison is ROC plots plus a convex-hull statement ('all but one point within this convex hull come from classifiers based on the Cluster-SMOTE method', p.5); figure not digitized
notes: Paper title in PDF: 'Combating Imbalance in Network Intrusion Datasets'. Proposed method: Cluster-SMOTE (k-means on minority class, SMOTE applied per cluster; variants '500 3 clusters SMOTE' and '500 5 clusters SMOTE' in Fig. 4). Evaluation: Packets 75%/25% stratified split; Destinations 10-fold CV with TP/FP rates averaged (p.5). Undersampling levels {1%MAJ, 5%MAJ, 10%MAJ, 20%MAJ, ..., 100%MAJ} (p.4). Loss ratio varied from 1 to .01 (p.5). Results only as ROC curves in Figs. 2-5; no supplementary file referenced.
